record.paper_title: The cosmological constant, dark matter, supersymmetry, and other unsolved problems from a fresh perspective
record.original_question: How should the 3-5 sigma experimental and observational anomalies that suggest extensions of both the standard model of particle physics and the standard model of cosmology be explained?

evidence.quote: 3 −5σ results of various experiments and observations which suggest that the standard models of both particle physics and cosmology need to be extended

artifact.self_contained_problem: Provide a theoretical framework that simultaneously explains the collection of experimental and observational anomalies, currently at the 3–5 standard-deviation level of statistical significance, which appear to require extensions of both the Standard Model of particle physics (e.g., the muon anomalous magnetic moment (g−2)_μ discrepancy, the W-boson mass measurement tension, lepton-flavor-universality-violation hints in semileptonic B-meson decays, and neutrino-sector anomalies) and the standard ΛCDM model of cosmology (e.g., the Hubble tension between local distance-ladder and CMB-inferred determinations of H₀, the S₈/σ₈ tension between weak-lensing and CMB-inferred large-scale structure amplitude, and other persistent anomalies in cosmological data). Specifically: construct a single, internally consistent extension of the Standard Model of particle physics and/or of ΛCDM that accounts quantitatively for these anomalies, makes falsifiable predictions for upcoming experiments, and is compatible with all existing precision constraints.
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2026, the listed 3–5σ anomalies (muon g−2, W-mass, B-decay LFU hints, Hubble and S₈ tensions, etc.) remain actively investigated with no unified, widely accepted explanation; some individual anomalies have shifted in significance with new data but no consensus BSM/cosmology extension has been established.

status_evidence.title: Muon g-2 and related anomalies status
status_evidence.snippet: Lists multiple 3-5 sigma anomalies in particle physics and cosmology that suggest extensions of both standard models.
status_evidence.claim: These anomalies are presented as unresolved open problems requiring explanation.
